en: Dhammapaccanīya (2), Dukatikapaṭṭhānapāḷi (3) 9.8. The Couplets on "Not Having a Cause" and "Having a Cause," and the Triplets on "The Wholesome" 9.8. Nahetusahetukaduka, Kusalattika (The Couplets on Not Having a Cause and Having a Cause;
the Triplets on the Wholesome) [Textual content omitted per instructions] [End of Section]

Dependent on a state that is neither a root, nor accompanied by a root, nor wholesome, there arises a state that is neither a root, nor accompanied by a root, nor wholesome, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated. There are nine [instances] for the root;
four for the object; five for the predominance … pe … six for mutuality … pe … two for prenascence and repetition … pe … nine for non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root, nor accompanied by a root, nor unwholesome, there arises a state that is neither a root, nor accompanied by a root, nor unwholesome, by way of the root condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to root-condition (hetu-paccaya), there are nine; with respect to object-condition (ārammaṇa-paccaya), four; with respect to predominance-condition (adhipati-paccaya), five ... pe ... with respect to mutuality-condition (aññamañña-paccaya), six ... pe ...

with respect to prenascence-condition (purejāta-paccaya) and repetition-condition (āsevana-paccaya), two ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance-condition (avigata-paccaya), nine. In dependence on a state that is neither-root, neither-rootless, and neither-indeterminate, there arises a state that is neither-root, neither-rootless, and neither-indeterminate by way of root-condition.
